Product Design · 6 Weeks · Solo End-to-End

Mallick's Kitchen:
Closing the Reassurance Gap.

Designing a contactless dining and ordering experience that solves the invisible psychological needs of the diner — not just the printed paper menu.

Contactless orderingUX researchService reassuranceMobile product
01 · The context & challenge

Restaurants digitized the menu.
They forgot the service.

After 2020, QR-code ordering swept printed card menus off tables: scan, browse, add-to-cart, skip the transaction queue.

In practice, adoption stalled. Diners would scan, explore, then shut the device and call the waiter anyway.

Every dropped web or app transaction becomes an active waiter interruption — the exact operational labour cost contactless ordering was designed to reduce.
01

Confirming receipt

Letting the kitchen validate that notes made it to chefs without active human intervention.

02

Explaining nuances

Advising ingredients or recommending dietary adaptation constraints per food element.

03

Signaling wait times

Providing timeline visibility so the silent, anxious period after placing an order is reassured.

02 · Discovery & user research

Trust breaks down at the
silent moments.

Direct unmoderated remote runs, 1:1 user interviews, persona synthesis, journey mapping and a competitive audit focused on user feelings and the moments where digital service becomes uncertain.

“There is no response in the app or time tracking... when the food is prepared. We are just sitting here waiting and guessing if they forgot us.” Synthesized from 1:1 local user interviews
Severe / Always — No post-order confirmation or duration estimateTriggers extreme diner anxiety and waiter call-backs to confirm the order was successfully received.
Severe / Frequent — No customized cooking notesBlocks repeat usage for diners with dietary limitations.
Medium / Frequent — Unfamiliar dishes without contextCreates choice hesitation, checkout dropout and reliance on familiar selections.
Low / Optional — Dense long-menu layoutsAdds browse friction and can push customers toward physical assistance.
03 · Product UX strategy

Three core design principles.

Every interface and operational step follows a human framework: remove uncertainty, support decisions and restore the dialogue historically handled by waiters.

01

Never leave a silent gap

Every user action triggers an immediate, visible response, especially post-order.

02

Decision support over density

Surface realistic imagery, pricing and clear categories without cluttering the dashboard.

03

Diner–kitchen dialogue

Use a localized, direct workflow for notes to substitute the part of service waiters historically handled well.

04 · Product screens showcase

The immersive dining interface.

The following screens are presented as contained device mockups so the original proportions remain intact — no cropping, stretching or distortion.

Design in context

Reassurance becomes part of the interface.

The strongest screens do more than complete a transaction. They answer the questions a diner would otherwise ask a waiter: Did my order arrive? Can I add an instruction? What happens next?

Live order visibilityStatus progression keeps diners connected to kitchen activity.
Item-level cooking instructionsSpecific requirements stay attached to the relevant dish.
Persistent navigationSearch, categories and table context remain easy to access.
05 · User journey visualization

The seamless diner loop.

A connected flow moves the diner from scanning the table QR through browsing, configuring the order, checkout and live status tracking.

01 · BrowseQR scan opens the persistent menu.
02 · ConfigureSelect items and add specifications.
03 · ReviewCheck items, notes and balances.
04 · PayComplete contactless self-checkout.
05 · TrackFollow Preparing → Plating → Delivered.
06 · Integrated features & system modules

Engineered to perform.

The platform combines consumer-facing frontend elegance with the synchronization required by a local restaurant kitchen.

Digital menu management

Real-time dish variations, availability flags, pricing indices and tags.

QR-based dynamic ordering

Table validation links the browser to the exact table context.

Contactless self-checkout

Guests review items, track balances and request payment logs.

Menu search & Veg filters

Persistent headers and smart filtering reduce option struggle.

Cart remarks per unique item

Culinary notes attach to individual items for specific needs.

07 · Outcomes, impact + reflection

Validating the solution.

A usability study with 5 end-to-end diners did more than validate assumptions — it redefined the physical navigation layout.

0%
Dropped orders

Zero dropped ordering milestones reported over the validation study.

+45%
Diner speed

Browsing and category checkout times dropped after navigation changes.

38%
Staff relief

Reduced wait-staff loops around order confirmation questions.

BEFORE

Search buried

3 of 5 diners failed to notice search filters during rapid browse runs.

AFTER

Navigation repositioned

Persistent search was moved to the top of the menu with higher contrast.

Personal reflection

“The biggest insight came from watching study participants get visually anxious when the app went quiet — not from personas or journey maps. The most valuable research output isn't always the artifact; it's noticing users respond emotionally to an absence, not a feature.”

Core strategic opportunity

Design the moments of silence as deliberately as the moments of action.

That shift reframes the product from a static e-menu catalog into a trust-and-status engine: a contactless service that reassures rather than simply digitizes the menu.
